full_judgment: 37. In Rahmat Ali v. M/S Banares Silk Industries & another, (1) the facts were that the plaintiff was a tenant under the Government, Defendant No. 2, with regard to a shop in the Government New Market at Dacca, in which, he allowed the defendant No. 1 to carry on a tailoring business temporarily as a licensee on the promise that he would vacate the said room when required by the plaintiff. The plaintiff revoked the license and desired the licensee, the defendant No. 1, to vacate the premises but the said defendant No. 1 did not do so on the other hand, he sought to get himself recognised as a tenant by the defendant No. 2, the Government. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed this suit for declaration of his title and for khas possession by evicting the defendant No. 1. He claimed no relief against the Government, defendant No. 2, and valued the suit at Rs.120/-, as according to the plaintiff, there was no objective standard of valuation and paid court-fee accordingly. The Defendant No. 1 contended that it was suit for possession after evicting a licensee and, as such, it was to be valued Under section 7(v) of the Act. The learned Munsif found that there was no specific provisions in the Court-fees Act for eviction of a licensee by a monthly tenant, and held that section 7 Cl. (xii) of the Act, was applicable and directed the plaintiff to value the suit in terms of that provision and to pay deficit court fee. The learned Single Judge hearing the matter on revision made by the defendant against the order of the learned Munsif recommended the matter to be settled by a Division Bench as according to him there was a clear divergence of opinion between the High Courts of India. Thereafter, the Division Bench before which it came up for hearing further recommended that the question be settled by a larger Bench as the matter involved a substantial question of law and divergent opinions expressed by different High Court on the question. It may be noted, no question was formulated for the decision of the Special Bench which on the facts as, stated above, dealt with as to what would be the appropriate valuation of the suit for the purpose of Court fee.
